Standard Lyc. ⲟⲩⲉⲉ = ⲟⲩⲁ 'one'; with ⲛⲟⲩⲱⲧ 'alone' forms standard Coptic 'one alone' construction. Trace of ⲉ̣ visible.
Word ⲧⲟⲩⲃⲟ 'purification' continues from line 1 ⲧⲟ̄|; ⲛⲧⲟ restored gives ⲧⲛ̄ⲧⲟⲩⲃⲟ 'the purification' as object of ⲁⲍⲱⲅⲣⲁⲫⲉ 'depict.'
ⲁⲍⲱⲅⲣⲁⲫⲉ ⲙⲙⲁⲥ idiom: 'depict her/it' with 3sg.f object suffix ⲙⲙⲁⲥ referring back to ⲧⲙⲉⲥⲟⲧⲏⲥ 'the mediation' (fem.). ⲙⲙⲁ restored at line start.
Greek loan ⲕⲁⲑⲁⲣⲓⲍⲉ < καθαρίζειν 'purify' continues from line 3 ⲛⲥⲉ-; standard editor's restoration.
Demonstrative ⲡⲓ- begins ⲡⲓⲕⲁⲧⲏⲭⲟⲩⲙⲉⲛⲟⲥ 'this catechumen' (line 5). Bracket on transcription marks ⲡⲓ as restored at line-end.
ⲧⲱⲧ in series with ⲁϩⲡⲉⲓⲑⲉ 'he was persuaded' and ⲁϩⲕⲁⲣⲱϩ 'he became silent' — three sequential verbs of acquiescence. ⲧⲱⲧ ⲛ̄ϩⲏⲧ 'be persuaded/agreed' is the standard idiom.

notes.decision: Translated 'Our Lord, why.' ⲡⲭⲉ likely Lyc. abbreviation/contraction of ⲡⲉⲛⲭⲁⲓⲥ 'our Lord' (cf. ⲡⲡⲛ̄ⲭⲁⲓ̈ⲥ in glossary), with the 1pl possessive ⲛ̄- elided. ⲉⲧⲃⲉ ⲉⲩ = 'why' (Lyc. ⲉⲩ for ⲟⲩ).

Read as the negative-perfect contrast: 'you have written every matter into the Icon, (yet) you have not written...' ⲙ̄ⲡⲉⲕ-ⲥϩⲁⲓ̈ = neg. perf. 2sg.m. The Icon (ⲍⲓⲕⲱⲛ) is Mani's pictorial book (the Eikōn / Picture-Book / Ārdhang), into which 'every matter' has been depicted. The disciples ask why the doctrine of catechumen-purification through metangismos is missing.

Greek loanword μεταγγισμός 'transmigration, transfusion (of soul into new body)' — standard Manichaean technical term for metempsychosis. The catechumens, lacking the elect's full purification, are purified through successive rebirths (cf. lines 16-17 'fall down again as a righteous one').

Translated 'stood on his feet, he said.' ⲧⲱⲕ ⲁⲣⲉⲧⲩ̄ = standard Coptic ⲧⲱⲕ ⲁⲣⲉⲧϥ̄/ⲱϩⲉ ⲉⲣⲁⲧϥ̄ 'stand on his feet, stand fast' (in glossary). The Lyc. ⲩ̄ for suffix -ϥ̄ is dialectal. ⲡⲁϫⲉϩ = ⲡⲉϫⲁϥ 'he said' (in glossary as ⲡⲁⲭⲉϩ, same root with -ϩ for -ϥ).
ⲟⲡ at the start of the page is the tail of a word continuing from the lost end of page 234. Possibly a remnant of ⲱⲡ 'count, reckon' or part of a compound; rendered as fragment '[...]op.'
Read as ⲁⲕ-ϣⲱⲡⲉ '(you) have come' (with Lyc. ⲁⲕ→ⲁ before ϣ), continuing the 2sg address to the Illuminator that runs through ⲁⲕⲟⲩⲱⲛⲍ̄, ⲁⲕⲍⲱⲣⲁⲫⲉ. The verb ϣⲱⲡⲉ ⲁ- 'come to' is standard.

Translated 'the Righteous one' on assumption that ⲡⲁⲓⲕⲁⲗⲟⲥ here = ⲡⲇⲓⲕⲁⲓⲟⲥ (Greek δίκαιος) with Lyc/scribal vowel shift ⲇⲓⲕⲁⲓ→ⲁⲓⲕⲁⲗ. Confirmed by context: this figure stands paired antithetically with ⲡⲣⲉϥⲣ̄ⲛⲁⲃⲉ 'the Sinner' in line 5 — the standard Manichaean righteous/sinner doublet for the soul-paths painted in the Picture-Book.
Read as ⲛ̄-ⲥⲉ-ⲧⲉϩⲟ 'and-they-cause-to-reach' (Lyc. ⲩ̄ for ⲥⲉ before ⲧ; cf. accumulated ⲧⲉϩⲟ 'reach, attain'). Causative-conjunctive: 'and they cause him to attain (the region of light).'
= ⲡⲣⲉϥ†ϩⲁⲡ 'the judge,' confirmed in glossary. Functions appositionally to the preceding ⲡⲕⲣⲓⲧⲏⲥ; the two terms (one Greek, one Coptic) name the same cosmic figure judging the dead.

Read as Lyc. ⲙⲟⲩϩⲉ 'burn, scorch' (Crum 207b) rather than ⲙⲟⲩϩ 'fill,' since the immediate cosmological context is Gehenna — the place of fire. The clause 'in which they habitually burn within forever' captures the eschatological torment proper to the Manichaean Gehenna.

3pl perfect 'they have painted' here functions impersonally/passively: 'these two have been painted' — referring back to the Righteous one and the Sinner the Illuminator depicted in the Great Icon. Could alternatively be a scribal slip for ⲁⲕⲍⲱⲣⲁⲫⲉ 'you have painted' (continuing the 2sg address); preserved as written.
Direct 2sg accusatorial question: 'But you — why have you not painted them?' The catechumen-disciple is challenging Mani directly about the asymmetry of the Picture-Book.

= ϩⲟ ϩⲓ ϩⲟ 'face by face / face-to-face' — the disciple's plea for direct visual recognition of the catechumen-soul's path within the icon, mirroring the categorical depictions of Righteous and Sinner.

The Illuminator's reply opens with a categorical denial: ⲙⲛ̄-ⲟⲁⲙ 'there is no power.' The reasoning given (lines 19-26) is that the catechumen's destiny varies place-by-place and depends on works performed with the Elect — too multiform to fix in a single image.
Read here as Greek ἐπειδή 'since, because,' introducing the causal clause justifying the impossibility. Distinct from the homograph ⲡⲉⲓⲁⲏ 'this end' (Lyc. ⲡⲉⲓ-ϩⲁⲏ).
= ϥⲥⲏϩ 'he is written/inscribed' (qualitative of ⲥϩⲁⲓ̈ 'write,' Lyc. ⲍ for ϩ, ⲩ for ϥ). The Elect's path is 'written in the icon' — affirming what was said in line 8 about the Righteous one.

ⲡⲉⲧⲉ ⲙⲛ̄ ⲃⲁⲙ + infinitive = standard Coptic impersonal 'that which there-is-no power to (do).' ⲙⲙⲁⲥ is 3sg.f object referring back to ⲧⲙⲉⲥⲟⲧⲏⲥ 'the mediation' (fem.). The catechumen's purification cannot be visually depicted because catechumens are not purified all in one place but dispersed.

Tentative parsing as ⲭⲁⲕ ⲙⲉϩ 'fully complete' or as a verb of fulfillment + ⲛ̄ϩⲏⲧ 'in heart' = 'fulfilled in heart.' Could alternatively be ⲭⲱⲕ-ⲙ̄ⲙⲁϩ 'complete (themselves).' The sense is that catechumens, lacking unified purification, also lack inward completion of heart.
